bio: My research began with molecular contacts and thin-film electrodes in organic and hybrid optoelectronics. I now study how interfaces, defects, and electronic and ionic transport shape memory-state formation, device variability, and reliability. First-author studies span molecular interface control, optoelectronic memristors, analog synapses, and printed-electronics variability.
vision: My current doctoral work investigates the precision limits of multilevel ionic memory through state-formation dynamics and low-frequency noise. Research on printed stretchable interconnects provides a parallel foundation in process variation and electrical reliability. Oxide electronics and integrated device platforms are directions I aim to develop from this experimental base.
